requirement:
An unmet file threshold or an unexecuted or not-measured function MAY satisfy
the coverage policy only
through current, accepted, independently assessed evidence explaining why its
coverage is incomplete. An exception MUST be attached to the source file or
function whose incomplete coverage it justifies. A file-threshold exception
MUST NOT automatically excuse untested functions.
An exception MUST NOT excuse another source item's incomplete coverage.
Changes to the source item, justification, or other inputs
of its citation review MUST invalidate the affected exception under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`.

A source comment or unassessed justification alone MUST NOT count as accepted
exception evidence. Function and gap identities MUST remain portable between
equivalent local and CI checkouts rather than depend on checkout paths,
run identifiers, timestamps, or process identifiers.
rationale:
The four supplied tests in `src/execution_coverage/check.rs` cover each obligation in `requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`. I also read `fn[exceptions]` to confirm that file-root and function citations go through one review-validation path. No gap remains.

- **Exception only through current, accepted, independent evidence.**
  - `missing_and_stale_explanations_fail_the_report` has the citations in source but no review. The report fails with "missing citation review; run `habeas author`". A review of `true` then makes it pass.
  - `accepted_file_and_function_explanations_remain_separate_from_execution` records review determination `false` and asserts "determination is false" and a failed report. It records `{"FIXME":[...]}` and asserts "cannot accept a {fixme}". So a source comment or unassessed justification alone does not count.
- **Exceptions attach to a file or function and excuse the right gaps.**
  - Zero-execution functions are excused: the function citation produces "- code.rs#fn[a]: zero execution" under the accepted exceptions.
  - Not-measured functions are excused ("#fn[a]: not measured").
  - An unmeasured file is excused ("code.rs: not measured — accepted exception").
  - The file-threshold shortfall is excused ("code.rs: file threshold (0/1 (0.0%))"), and the 0.0% figure is not raised.
- **A file-threshold exception MUST NOT excuse untested functions.** The first phase of `accepted_file_and_function_explanations_remain_separate_from_execution` has only a file citation. The report fails with "#fn[a]: zero execution".
- **An exception MUST NOT excuse another source item's gap.** `function_explanations_never_transfer_to_other_functions_or_the_file` covers two cases.
  - An outer-function citation waives only `fn[outer]`. `fn[outer]/fn[inner]` and `fn[sibling]` still require exceptions.
  - An inner-function citation waives only the inner function. The outer function and the sibling still require exceptions.
  - In both cases the file threshold still shows FAIL, and another file's unmeasured gap is not excused.
- **Invalidation when the item, justification or other inputs change.**
  - `missing_and_stale_explanations_fail_the_report` changes the rationale, which gives "citations changed". It then changes the function body, which gives "outline input changed". In both cases the function gap is no longer waived.
  - `standard_inline_doc_and_fenced_commentary_reviews_track_their_explanations` changes a doc-comment rationale and a fenced rationale. The exceptions become unaccepted and errors are reported.
  - File-root and function citations share the review-validation path in `fn[exceptions]`, so the function-level stale checks also exercise the file-root logic.
  - Staleness caused by a change to the cited built-in text belongs to the citation-review requirement's own tests, so it needs no test here.
- **Portable identities.** `standard_inline_doc_and_fenced_commentary_reviews_track_their_explanations` copies the review JSON into a fresh checkout at a different temporary path. The exception is accepted with no errors. The report identities are project-relative (`code.rs#fn[a]`). Results recorded in the other tests carry different run labels, and the identities and outcomes do not change.

The other requirements with `{test}` sites on these functions (`.reviews`, `.binding`, `.author`) are assessed separately.

text: :::{req} check.exceptions
An unmet file threshold or an unexecuted or not-measured function MAY satisfy
the coverage policy only
through current, accepted, independently assessed evidence explaining why its
coverage is incomplete. An exception MUST be attached to the source file or
function whose incomplete coverage it justifies. A file-threshold exception
MUST NOT automatically excuse untested functions.
An exception MUST NOT excuse another source item's incomplete coverage.
Changes to the source item, justification, or other inputs
of its citation review MUST invalidate the affected exception under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`.
A source comment or unassessed justification alone MUST NOT count as accepted
exception evidence. Function and gap identities MUST remain portable between
equivalent local and CI checkouts rather than depend on checkout paths,
run identifiers, timestamps, or process identifiers.
:::{req} citation_review
Every source item outside the book that carries at least one `{cite}` reference
other than a citation of `habeas:util` under {cite}`requirements.references.util`
MUST have a citation review: an assessment of that item's citations, recorded at
`evidence/citations/<file>/<selector>.json`, where `<file>` is the item's
project-relative path, `<selector>` is its outline selector with every `/` and
`%` percent-encoded, and the root node uses `_root`. The review MUST use the
prompt defined by {cite}`requirements.authoring.citation_prompt`. For citations
of project requirements and examples, the reviewer MUST assess whether the item
should be re-checked or kept in sync when the cited definition changes, and
whether the reference procedure of
{cite}`requirements.references.procedure` calls for `{impl}` or `{test}` instead.
For citations of built-ins, the reviewer MUST check the permitted reference
roles and forms and any citation-review criteria stated in the built-in's fixed
text, using the item's source and commentary. A permitted citation role alone
MUST NOT suffice when the fixed text states additional criteria. Mandatory inputs,
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, MUST be the item's outline
node, each cited declaration or built-in text, and the citations' commentary. The record MUST contain the item's file and selector,
its citations by role, name, and commentary, `determination`, `rationale`, and
`inputs`, with determinations under {cite}`requirements.ci.outcomes`. Validation
MUST require a current, accepted review for every such item and report stale,
missing, or orphaned reviews; a review MUST become stale when the item's hash,
a cited declaration, or its citations or their commentary change. Authoring with
`--all` MUST include citation reviews, and `habeas author citations:<file>#<selector>`
MUST author the review of the one item it names, under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`, where omitting `#<selector>`
names the file's root node. A citation in a requirement or example
declaration is reviewed as part of that definition's own assessment instead.
Fenced commentary elsewhere in the book is reviewed under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review.book_commentary`.
Storage MAY use the versioned representation under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.habeas.evidence_format`, retaining the same review
information and validation rules.
